strings.name: Rupert Murdoch
strings.role: Media entrepreneur · Chairman emeritus of News Corp and Fox
strings.summary: Rupert Murdoch expanded from Australian newspapers into Britain and the United States, building international publishing, film, television and subscription-media businesses. He developed Fox while facing sustained controversy over media concentration, political influence and journalism ethics. He became chairman emeritus of News Corp and Fox in 2023; the family settled its trust-control dispute in 2025.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026, including 2026 corporate filings. The timeline includes the 2025 trust settlement and retains controversies such as phone hacking. Influence does not endorse journalism ethics or political positions.
strings.influence.rationale: Built international news and television companies with lasting influence on media industries and public information.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education or early career
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Worcester College, Oxford; studied philosophy, politics and economics
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: International media business
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Built cross-border news and entertainment operations through newspaper acquisitions and broadcasting investment.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Television and news markets
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Developed the Fox network and Fox News, substantially influencing television and public information.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Family-trust settlement
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Family members agreed control arrangements that strengthened Lachlan’s position in the group.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Becomes chairman emeritus
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Stepped down as chairman of both companies. Lachlan became sole chair of News Corp and continued as executive chair and CEO of Fox.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Fox reaches civil settlement with Dominion
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Fox Corp and Fox News agreed to pay $787.5 million to settle Dominion’s defamation lawsuit over coverage of false claims of fraud in the 2020 US election.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Entertainment assets sold to Disney
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Most 21st Century Fox entertainment assets went to Disney; Fox Corporation retained news, sports and other operations.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: News of the World closes
strings.timeline.event-4.text: The paper closed as the phone-hacking scandal widened, intensifying debate on ethics and governance.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Fox News launches
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Launched the US cable news channel, expanding television news operations.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Fox broadcast network launches
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Used television-station assets to enter the US national network market.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: British newspaper acquisitions
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Gained control of News of the World and The Sun, accelerating international expansion.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Enters family newspaper business
strings.timeline.event-8.text: After inheriting his father’s interests, became publisher of Adelaide’s The News and a company director.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in Melbourne
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Grew up in a newspaper family and later studied at Oxford.
